summary.headline: EFC (I) Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 30% YoY to ₹332 crore, with PAT up 36% to ₹77 crore and EBITDA margin near 40%.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about ₹332 crore versus ~₹255 crore a year earlier (+30%), with EBITDA of ~₹134 crore (+21%) and PAT of ~₹77 crore (+36%). H1 FY27 revenue was ~₹650 crore (+30%) and PAT ~₹148 crore (+43%), with EPS of ₹10.11 versus ₹7.09. Management outlined a proposed demerger of the leased-premise managed office business into the listed parent and the acquisition of Ultrafresh Modular Solutions via a share swap. Design & Build growth lagged the 50-60% annual target in H1, which management attributed to order book timing.

segments.name: Leasing (managed workspace)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ~₹168 crore (+30% YoY); H1 ~₹322 crore vs ₹252 crore. Management cites occupancy consistently above 90%, with no change quarter on quarter or year on year.

segments.name: Design & Build (turnkey contracting)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ~₹129 crore (+16% YoY); H1 ~₹230 crore vs ₹196 crore. Management targets 50-60% growth for FY27 and cites an order book of more than ₹300 crore.

segments.name: Furniture Manufacturing (Ek Design)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ~₹35 crore (+149% YoY); H1 ~₹63 crore vs ₹27 crore. Growth is from a small base, and management plans to improve capacity utilisation and inventory management.

guidance_outlook: Management says it is on track for annual targets across all three verticals and expects a stronger H2, consistent with prior years.
Design & Build FY27 growth target of 50-60% reaffirmed, supported by the order book, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be promising.

Long-term margin guidance: consolidated EBITDA above 20%; Leasing ~25% at corporate level and ~30% at centre level; Design & Build 18-22%; Furniture ~24-25% at optimal capacity; integrated margin 20-22% on an annualised basis.
Quarterly margins may fluctuate due to project execution cycles and expense timing; management said annualised margins will hold.
Design & Build working capital cycle guided at roughly 60-90 days (earlier 90-120 days), with retention around 5% of project value.
Demerger subject to NCLT and other approvals; management is confident of approval soon.
Ultrafresh acquisition expected to be EPS-accretive over the long term; integration and synergies are the immediate focus.
capex_capacity: Ultrafresh Modular Solutions acquired for ~₹54 crore via share swap at ₹270 per share, about 1.49x FY26 revenue; it has a manufacturing facility at Nalagarh, Himachal Pradesh, and more than 160 touch points across Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

Proposed demerger filed with NCLT: the leased-premise managed office business moves into listed EFC (I) Ltd, and owned property stays in wholly owned subsidiary EFC Limited. Project-specific SPVs in Leasing are to fold into the listed entity.
Owned real estate is about 8-10% of the leasing portfolio; the company said it monetised a Pune property through an asset sale and leaseback, earning a 39-40% return on capital.
Management said it is evaluating further opportunities while maintaining capital allocation discipline.
demand_pricing: India office absorption was about 66 million sq ft in the first nine months of 2026, per management; the Indian furniture market is cited at ₹25-29 billion.
Enterprises and GCCs are prioritising flexible, managed workspace that avoids large upfront capex.
Management said material and service prices rose substantially in Q2, adding some margin pressure.
Pricing and quotations for internal group business are set competitively, with big-four firms used for arm's-length benchmarking.

qa_highlights.question: Pramod Mohan: What is portfolio occupancy across mature and new centres, and will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Nikhil Bhuta said occupancy is consistently above 90% and stable quarter on quarter and year on year, and expects this to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Pramod Mohan: Will consolidated margins normalise as Design & Build and Furniture grow in mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are sustainable, with a consolidated EBITDA target above 20% and an integrated 20-22% annualised, while quarterly margins may vary.

qa_highlights.question: Pramod Mohan: What was the Sanvritti Alpha transaction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a Pune property bought about a year earlier, redeveloped and fitted out, then sold to an investor on an asset sale and leaseback basis, with the company remaining operating partner. It said this generated a 39-40% return on capital and helps repay asset-backed debt (LRD/LAP).

qa_highlights.question: Sahil Singh: Can Design & Build reach 50-60% growth given H1 growth of only 16-17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on target, citing an order book above ₹300 crore and expecting Q3 and Q4 to be strong, and that quarterly numbers are not the right indicator.

qa_highlights.question: Sahil Singh: Why did EBITDA grow 21% when revenue grew 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to timing differences in leasing development costs and revenue recognition and to sharp increases in material and service prices in the quarter, saying annualised margins will hold.

qa_highlights.question: Vishal Kunden: What was the rationale for the ₹54 crore Ultrafresh share swap and its valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited northern manufacturing access, the Tier 2 and Tier 3 distribution network, and modular product expansion. It said the deal was valued at about 1.49x FY26 revenue, with shares valued at ₹270 each by big-four valuers, and expects EPS accretion over time.

qa_highlights.question: Ashutosh Chaudhary: Could receivables and working capital grow disproportionately as Design & Build scales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working-capital intensive but not disproportionate. Cycles are around 60-90 days depending on project, with retention about 5% of project value and milestone-based billing for institutional clients.

qa_highlights.question: Shailendra: What is the rationale for the demerger, its structure, timeline and arm's-length dealing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the demerger separates asset-light leasing (into the listed parent) from owned property (in EFC Limited) to give clearer capital allocation and ROCE. Related-party pricing is said to be arm's length, benchmarked by big-four firms and reported to SEBI.

risks_watch: Design & Build H1 growth of 16-17% against the 50-60% full-year target. Watch whether Q3 and Q4 close the gap.
Q2 EBITDA growth (21%) lagged revenue growth (30%). Watch whether margins recover as guided.
Working capital and receivables as Design & Build scales; watch debtor days and retention balances.
Pending NCLT approval for the demerger, plus its cost and timeline, which were not quantified on the call.
Ultrafresh integration risk and the dilution from the share swap.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth and margins, but defensive when questioned on the Design & Build target gap and the margin trend, where it repeatedly redirected to annualised figures. Answers on related-party pricing and the demerger were long and general, with few specifics on cost or timeline.
key_quotes: Our ambition is not simply to build a larger EFC, but to build a stronger, more competitive and more valuable EFC, one that delivers consistent performance and create long-term value for all stakeholders.
So we are absolutely confident on achieving the targets that have been set.
Margin comparison should happen on an annualized level.
So believe this is absolutely EPS-accretive transactions in the long-term.

adds.what: Ultrafresh Modular Solutions manufacturing facility at Nalagarh, Himachal Pradesh (acquired via share swap, ~Rs 54 crore)

growth.why: Management reaffirmed a 50-60% FY27 Design & Build growth target backed by an order book of over Rs 300 crore, though D&B grew only 16% in Q2 and 1H lagged that target; leasing occupancy is steady at about 90%, and the Ultrafresh acquisition adds a Nalagarh facility and 160+ touch points.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA grew 21% vs revenue 30% and margin was ~40%, with management guiding integrated 20-22% annualised but citing sharp material and service price rises in Q2, so expansion is conditional on recovery.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Ultrafresh adds a Nalagarh facility (commissioned, minor) and 160+ touch points, but no new greenfield capacity or timed plant was guided; leasing occupancy steady at ~90%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Group revenue grew 30% in Q2 and H1 (~₹650 crore), Leasing grew 30% with occupancy above 90%, and D&B order book exceeds ₹300 crore backing a reaffirmed 50-60% FY27 target, though D&B grew only 16% in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation signal is occupancy ~90%, but the company is asset-light in leasing, the Ultrafresh facility was acquired rather than built, and management stressed capital allocation discipline with no new capex announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reaffirmed rather than raised guidance (D&B 50-60%, EBITDA >20%), and it lagged its own D&B target in H1 at 16-17%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: D&B H1 growth of 16-17% against a 50-60% FY27 target needs a sharp H2 step-up, and Q2 EBITDA lagged revenue, so a target cut is possible if Q3 and Q4 do not close the gap.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cited modular product expansion via Ultrafresh and Furniture is growing 149% from a small base (₹35 crore in Q2), but no specific launch dates were given.

rows.label: Demerger of leased-premise business into listed EFC (I) Ltd
rows.why: Demerger filed with NCLT and management is confident of approval soon, though cost and timeline were not quantified.

rows.label: Ultrafresh Modular Solutions share-swap integration
rows.why: Acquisition for ~₹54 crore at ₹270 per share (~1.49x FY26 revenue) is already done, with integration and synergies the immediate focus and EPS accretion expected over the long term.

rows.label: D&B working capital cycle improvement
rows.why: Cycle guided down to 60-90 days from 90-120 days with retention around 5%, though management also said working capital is intensive.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 50-60% D&B target, occupancy above 90% and margins, but was defensive on the H1 D&B growth gap and the Q2 EBITDA lag, repeatedly pointing to annualised figures; analysts pressed on D&B growth, margin gap and related-party pricing.
